audit_metadata.scope: Independent audit of the threshold-transfer study
audit_metadata.method: Re-implement matching and metric accumulation from scratch; do not call src/metrics.evaluate_detections. Compare to artifacts/threshold_transfer.json. No model inference re-run.
audit_metadata.verdict: PASS — study is methodologically defensible, ready to share.

byte_duplicate_pair_details.note: train has 16 Cars; val has 15 Cars
train has 1 Truck; val has 2 Trucks

implementation_audit.empty_GT_handling: 0 of 202 heldout images have empty GT; evaluate_detections excludes empty-GT classes from mAP
implementation_audit.rng_reproducibility: single random.Random(20261012) shared across FRCNN then YOLO then detector-vs-detector draws; re-implementing with the same RNG usage produces exact-match CI bounds and means to 6 decimal places

bootstrap_recomputation.ci_interpretation: 95% CIs are paired image-level bootstrap (500 reps, seed 20261012); they describe uncertainty in the F1 estimate on the 202-image heldout sample under image-level resampling, not on a deployment population. They are not a hypothesis test.

dev_best_f1_threshold_stability_under_de.note: FRCNN's chosen 0.60 is sharply stable. YOLO's 0.20 is less sharply defined: 28% of dev bootstraps pick 0.15, reflecting a flat F1 surface in the 0.15-0.25 range.

f1_sensitivity_to_threshold_within_pm_0..note: Maximum F1 swing within ±0.05 of chosen threshold is 0.005 (FRCNN dev) and 0.013 (YOLO heldout). The 0.05 grid is fine enough for the headline claim.

post_hoc_finer_grid_check_exploratory.label: exploratory — not used to retroactively change the preregistered 0.05 grid

1_confirmed_defects_requiring_fixes.verdict: None. Every numerical result in artifacts/threshold_transfer.json reproduces to 6 decimal places when matching and metric accumulation are re-implemented from scratch. The bootstrap is correctly implemented. The data split is correctly defined. No code change is required to the study artefacts.

items.change: Add a 'What the CIs estimate' note that the 95% CIs are paired image-level bootstrap 95% CIs from 500 replicates describing uncertainty on this specific 202-image held-out sample, not on a deployment population and not a hypothesis test.

Refine the strongest-finding paragraph to report the absolute dev→held-out F1 difference (+0.0092 for FRCNN, +0.0101 for YOLO) and the relative percentage (+1.4% / +1.8%) instead of the looser 'essentially without degradation' phrase.

Add a new § 7 'Exploratory post-hoc analyses' documenting the 0.01-grid sweep (YOLO 0.18 vs 0.20, dev F1 difference 0.0018) and the dev-bootstrap stability. Update § 8 'Conclusion' to include the absolute dev→held-out F1 differences and the explicit CI interpretation.

items.name: 0.01-grid dev sweep
items.finding: FRCNN's dev-best-F1 threshold is unchanged at 0.60. YOLOv8n's would have been 0.18 (F1=0.5693) instead of 0.20 (F1=0.5675), a dev-F1 difference of 0.0018. The YOLO dev-F1 surface is flat in 0.15-0.25.

items.name: Dev-best-F1 threshold stability under dev bootstrap (200 reps)
items.finding: FRCNN's chosen 0.60 wins 91% of dev bootstraps. YOLOv8n's chosen 0.20 wins 72%, with 0.15 winning 28% — consistent with the flat YOLO dev-F1 surface.

items.name: Hash + pixel-level duplicate verification
items.finding: SHA-1 of every image's raw bytes was computed for all 1,027 images. Only the 4 documented pairs overlap between dev and heldout. Pixel equality verified (max |diff|=0).

canonical_verdict.one_sentence: The threshold-transfer study is methodologically defensible and ready to share publicly.
canonical_verdict.scope: Based on the audit of the four phases (data split, metric recomputation, bootstrap, threshold-transfer conclusion) and the machine-readable cross-check in this file. No model inference was re-run; the audit used cached per-image predictions only.
